transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

Well, I'm here because I'm having a really hard time with my eating. What scares me is that once I start eating, especially when I'm alone in the kitchen... it feels like I've just stepped aside. I can't make myself stop. Even though I'm telling myself the whole time, like, 'Janet, just put it away,' I just can't do it.
After these episodes happen, do you do anything to try to compensate for what you ate or prevent weight gain, such as making yourself throw up, taking laxatives, or exercising excessively?

No, I don't do anything like that. I don't make myself throw up or take laxatives, and I definitely don't exercise excessively. I just... I usually just sit there feeling really awful and guilty about what I just did, but I don't try to get rid of the food or anything.
Could you tell me what your current height and weight are?

I'm actually not sure right now. I haven't stepped on a scale in quite a while... I've just been avoiding it, to be honest. And I don't really know my exact height off the top of my head either. I just don't have those exact numbers for you today.
Has anyone, like a doctor, family member, or friend, expressed concern that you are dangerously underweight or too thin?
No, definitely not. Nobody has ever said I was too thin or underweight. So, no, I haven't had anyone express that kind of concern.
About how often do these episodes where you feel unable to stop eating happen?

Let's see... looking back at my kitchen calendar and, you know, keeping track of my food bank weeks, I'd say they happen most weeks. Usually it's about once or twice a week. And it's been going on like that for many months now.
